t: Section 7(a) of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, as amended (33 U.S.C. 466 et seq.), is amended by striking “and for the three-month period ending September 30, 1971, $2,500,000.” and inserting in lieu thereof “and for the four-month period ending October 31, 1971, $4,000,000.”

fable.w: This section only amends an authorization of appropriations, extending the period and raising the dollar amount. The tempting reading is that the Federal Water Pollution Control Act involves state grant programs, but nothing in this text calls for consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: is amended by striking “and for the three-month period ending September 30, 1971, $2,500,000.” and inserting in lieu thereof “and for the four-month period ending October 31, 1971, $4,000,000.”

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely technical amendment to an appropriations statute, changing the amount of funding and the time period for which it is available. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or requirements for state/local input mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Section 7(a) of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, as amended (33 U.S.C. 466 et seq.), is amended by striking “and for the three-month period ending September 30, 1971, $2,500,000.” and inserting in lieu thereof “and for the four-month period ending October 31, 1971, $4,000,000.”

opus.w: This amendment only changes a funding period and dollar amount in Section 7(a) of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. Section 7 deals with grants to state water pollution programs, which might make it look like outsiders are involved. But grants are excluded from the definition, and this text only changes the money available. Nothing here involves an outside party in a federal decision.
opus.s: is amended by striking “and for the three-month period ending September 30, 1971, $2,500,000.” and inserting in lieu thereof “and for the four-month period ending October 31, 1971, $4,000,000.”

qwen_chat.w: This section is a purely fiscal amendment that adjusts the amount of appropriated funds and the time period for which they are available. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. There is no interaction with parties outside the federal government described in this text.
qwen_chat.s: Section 7(a) of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, as amended (33 U.S.C. 466 et seq.), is amended by striking “and for the three-month period ending September 30, 1971, $2,500,000.” and inserting in lieu thereof “and for the four-month period ending October 31, 1971, $4,000,000.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing funding levels affects public participation indirectly, but the text itself contains no procedural requirements for public input, consultation, or hearings. It is purely a fiscal amendment.
